title: Think, Plan, Paint: Layout-Aware Reasoning for Controllable Image Generation in Unified Models
claim: One model reasons, plans a layout, and renders images, and the same layout interface also supports user control and editing.
layout: 4 panels in a 2x2-style grid, dashed dividers, chat-bubble dialogues
description: The figure is a collage of four chat-style panels, each with a dark teal title banner. Panel 1, 'Image Generation: Think, Plan, Paint', is on the left. A user prompt (cow, calf and dog in a pasture) sits in a beige bubble beside a brown user icon. Below it, a robot labeled ATLAS (Thinking) gives step-by-step reasoning text. ATLAS (Planning) outputs a layout of colored bounding boxes. ATLAS (Painting) outputs the final photo. Panel 2, 'Fine-grained Control', shows the user editing the box layout and ATLAS returning a revised image. Panels 3 and 4, both titled 'Image Editing', show the instructions 'Add an orange cat above the dog' and 'Remove the calf'. Each panel pairs a before image with an after image. The eye goes first to the cow photos and the user bubbles.
caption: Our ATLAS framework generates images following a human-like Think, Plan, and Paint paradigm, and supports interleaved image generating and editing. Additionally, the Think and Plan phases provide the user with fine-grained control over the generation process.
abstract: Unified Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) offer a promising paradigm for unifying visual understanding and generation, yet they still struggle to follow complex spatial instructions and logical constraints in controllable image generation. To address this gap, we present ATLAS, a unified framework that equips MLLMs with a human-like "Think, Plan, and Paint" paradigm. We adopt layout as the shared representation that connects the three stages, enabling the model to reason about spatial requirements, plan explicit object arrangements, and render the final image. We further improve plan-to-image fidelity with reinforcement-learning-based layout alignment. We instantiate ATLAS at 7B and 80B scales, achieving state-of-the-art performance among MLLMs on image generation benchmarks and an average 65.31% improvement over existing layout-based unified MLLMs. On spatially related tasks, ATLAS obtains an average 23.06% gain over the base models. Through the same layout interface, ATLAS also supports instruction-guided editing and multimodal grounding. We further introduce ATLAS-Reasoning, a benchmark for evaluating generation under complex spatial instructions.
